title: Grape and apple bircher with hazelnuts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, sultanas, cinnamon, oranges, apples, grapes and hazelnuts are all plain whole foods with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco or similar, and 50g of hazelnuts is not a treat purchase.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a jug and a grater, plus squeezing oranges by hand and halving grapes, all easy for a beginner.

works.reason: 200g oats soaked in 400ml water plus the juice of two oranges gives a sensible bircher texture for four, and there is a step to loosen it if it is too stiff.

honest_times.reason: Juicing, grating two apples, halving 300g of grapes and chopping nuts fits within 15 minutes hands-on, and 490 minutes total covers the 8-hour soak.

honest_ingredients.reason: Sultanas matches the raisins-or-sultanas id, every listed ingredient is used in the steps, and the steps use nothing unlisted.

seasonal_feel.reason: Grapes and apples are both on the November list and make up the bulk of the bowl, and overnight oats is a fair cool-weather breakfast.

plain_voice.reason: It reads as clear, friendly British English with simple steps and no restaurant language or health preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, whole fruit and nuts make a filling, real-food breakfast that is not reliant on added sugar.
